agree.reason: The draft accepts the staff's stock numbers and sounds reasonable, but it gives commissioners nothing they haven't heard from other captains: no trip logs, no reporting-app offer, no worked-out alternative that meets the conservation goal.

honest.reason: It wisely drops the claim that every boat will close, but 'never got back to 170' goes beyond the brief's data, and it adds options the captain never offered: a separate for-hire limit, and 'a shorter time frame' where he had said a shorter season.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the 32 lost trips into about $29,000 and puts the survey at nearly 60%, but it never projects the three-year cost, never states the 2016 drop as a 19% decline, and leaves out that two captains would sell and that 70% of this season is already booked.

right_comparison.reason: It gives the 2016 drop and the partial recovery to 155, but it slants the trend with an unsupported 'never got back,' and its 9% versus 80% point is muddled, since a uniform cut mostly falls on private boats.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is a vague 'review after one season' with no measure or consequence; it never uses the checkable commitments that were available, such as trip logs from 2016 on or a reporting-app test next season.

objections.reason: It meets 'trust the staff numbers' by accepting them, but it doesn't show how a 3-fish limit or shorter season would still rebuild the stock, and the 'saves comparatively few fish' argument invites an easy rebuttal.

fit.reason: At about 330 words it fits a two-minute spoken comment and is laid out as remarks from the podium.
